# DotPagination

A row of round dots marking position in a carousel or slideshow. Knockout styling (white dots) — built for dark and media surfaces.

## Decisions

- ⏳ **open** `dp-version-unstamped` `medium confidence` (unowned): The Figma component carries s2a:meta version 0.0.0 with an empty changelog, so the contract has no version to mirror. Stamp it 1.0.0 in Figma and re-extract?
- ✅ decided `dp-count-booleans` `high confidence` (unowned): Figma exposes five booleans (Show Dot 1–5); the code exposes one `count`. Which is the contract's API? → count. The booleans are a Figma authoring affordance — a component there cannot vary its child count, so the same decision is spelled five ways. No consumer rebuilding this would implement showDot3; they would implement count. The booleans stay visible in the Figma evidence and in the prop notes rather than in the API.
- ✅ decided `dp-dot-internal` `high confidence` (unowned): Figma builds the dots from a separate `Dot` component set. Should Dot be its own contract, and the dots a slot? → No. The Dot set lives in a Figma section named "🚫 Internal — Do not use directly", so the design file already treats it as an implementation detail. Code has no Dot component at all — the dot is a part with one class. Modelled as a repeated part, not a slot.
- ✅ decided `dp-anatomy-repeat` `high confidence` (unowned): Five explicit parts (.dot-1 … .dot-5) as the docs sheet lists them, or one repeated part? → One part. Anatomy selectors are checked against classes the template and stylesheet actually define, and there is exactly one (.c-dot-pagination__dot). Five parts would name four selectors that do not exist. The Figma naming is recorded on the part instead.
- ✅ decided `dp-knockout-only` `high confidence` (unowned): Is there an on-light treatment? → No. The Figma component is knockout-only — white dots for dark and media surfaces — and no on-light variant exists in the set. Do not invent one; if a light surface needs pagination, that is a new request, not a variant.

## Accessibility

WCAG 2.2 AA: `2.1.1`, `2.4.7`, `2.5.8`, `4.1.2`

- `Tab`: moves focus through the dots, one stop each
- `Enter / Space`: selects that slide when onSelect is wired
- Dots are real <button> elements inside a <nav> landmark — keyboard operable (2.1.1).
- Active dot carries aria-current='true'; each dot has an aria-label naming its slide (4.1.2).
- Focus ring uses focus-ring/knockout for visibility on the dark surfaces this component targets (2.4.7).
- 8px hit area is below the 24px target-size guideline (2.5.8 AA) — acceptable as an inline indicator, but pair with adjacent prev/next controls for primary navigation.
